# What's known about one thing

After a Cursor plugin install, the short command loop is [plugins/crav1/README.md](../plugins/crav1/README.md).

When the user asks for startup options, that ask names only `$crav1-spark-to-spec`, `$crav1-ideas-to-spec`, `$crav1-bundle-to-specs`, `$crav1-existing-to-specs`, `$crav1-read-environment`, and `$crav1-fix-bug`.

[Explain](from-explain-existing-system.md) (`$crav1-explain-existing-system`) reads `docs/system/` first.

## First prompt

Name the thing, or `@` a spec folder or a code folder.

```text
$crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this

What's the status of <the feature, slice, or resource>? What's pending?
```

```text
$crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this
@docs/specs/<slug>/
```

A name matches first as written (`fn-market-data`, a slug, a title). An `@` keeps the search inside that path.

If the message has no name, no sentence, and no `@`, the command stops.

Pasted minutes go to `$crav1-add-to-spec`. A long dump goes to `$crav1-add-to-spec`.

## Reports (1.104.0)

Add one word to get a fixed report as a `.md` file instead of the free-form answer:

```text
$crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this report-feature-full xbid
$crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this report-change-short pr74
$crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this report-build-full @docs/specs/<slug>/
$crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this report-playbook-short CC Process 1.0
$crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this report-data-model-full orders
```

| Word | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| `report-feature-short` | Verdict, what it is, how it works, one flow diagram |
| `report-feature-full` | Every section: flows, C4 levels 1–2 (3 when described), deployment, decisions, delivery, live state |
| `report-change-short` | Verdict, 30-second version, what changes, one diagram |
| `report-change-full` | Architecture, branches, pipelines, the change, the discussion, open decisions; C4 only when architecture or pipelines matter |
| `report-build-short` | Status and the next tasks in dependency order |
| `report-build-full` | Every gap, the unblock order wave by wave, the task graph |
| `report-playbook-short` | Preview (1.109.0). Kept, Needs your answer (questions and spec conflicts, recommended + why), Compose, every kit step in order, an order diagram |
| `report-playbook-full` | Preview (1.109.0). Where it stands, the three buckets, every kit step, the order diagram, gaps no skill covers; then asks *Walk through it now?* (1.116.0) |
| `report-playbook-walk` | 1.116.0. Resumes the walk in chat at the first unanswered item of an existing playbook report |
| `report-data-model-full` | 1.118.0, export shape 1.121.0. One review of a saved data model, built from the saved records. Markdown and a PDF with the same prose and the diagrams drawn by name. It does not model again |

The file goes to your Downloads folder when the agent can reach it, otherwise a temp folder, and the chat always links it.

Any **Conflict:** line in the covered specs is listed under Needs your answer as C1, C2, …, with both sides and a recommended answer. An early step answers the questions and settles the conflicts with `$crav1-resolve-open-questions`, whenever you come back, and names every N and C it covers. Kept, Needs your answer and conflict items are bullet blocks, not tables, each with a plain `Answer:` or `Change:` line right under it, so you can fill the file yourself or send it to people who do not use the kit; read it back with `$crav1-resolve-open-questions apply <file>`, which checks what changed in the specs since the report and asks about any clash before writing.

**Walk it in chat (1.116.0, chat 1.117.0).** After `report-playbook-full` writes the file, it asks *Walk through it now?*. On yes, it first offers to settle the answers that block several steps (for example the merge order; `skip` takes them in order), then walks in Steps order, one item at a time, each with a short *Why this matters* (where it came from, what it changes) and the recommendation. Reply `yes`, your own answer, `more` for the full background, or add what you know; jump with `go to N9`. The chat states each item in words and does not use the report's item ids, not even in parentheses. You can also ask back, push back or change direction: it redrafts only Compose, Merge order and Steps as needed. When what you say and the record do not match, it works out the outcome you want from the known facts and your words, one follow-up at a time, then summarizes and waits for an explicit yes before it writes. Each clear answer is saved into the report, and nothing touches a spec during the walk. It does not start help, and it does not run pr-status. At the end you get a summary and one card: `yes (Recommended)` runs `$crav1-resolve-open-questions apply`, which writes only the filled confirmed lines and copies a filled playbook to `docs/playbooks/<topic>.md`. Typed changes go on that card's free-text answer. Stop any time and resume with `report-playbook-walk`. That resume also accepts a `docs/playbooks/` path. A headless run never walks; it writes the file and says how to resume. A short playbook still does not walk.

It does not say `table above` unless that table is in the reply.

## Steps

| Phase | You | Agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Question | A name, a sentence or two, an `@`, or a focus | Stops when nothing was named. Does not scan the repo to pick a thing |
| Match | — | One pass. Exact name first, then key words. Spec titles and Match quotes weigh highest. One winner, or a list to choose from |
| Slice | Read the answer | The spec, the plan, the tasks, Match, and open questions. The path is named |
| No slice | Read what is known | Repo, code, and environment notes. A candidate slice. Names spark, ideas, or intake. Does not run it |
| Live | Yes or no when a resource is prod-only | Azure settings and recent changes. Azure DevOps work items, open pull requests, and branches. Each fact is a live read. Never data |
| Live failed | Retry or Skip | One prompt. Skip is the repo-only answer, with why the live checks did not run |
| Stop | Glance | Writes nothing in the project, except a filled playbook copied on apply. Does not start Specify, Plan, or Build |

## What gets written

On apply, a filled playbook is copied to `docs/playbooks/<topic>.md`. `report-data-model-full` writes one new snapshot under the saved model, `report.md` and `report.pdf`, and does not edit the model.

No `plan.md`. No `tasks.md`.

A guess is labeled `(inference, not in the docs)`.

`$crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this` answers a named slice from the skill file. No matching slice, and a `report-` word, each open one references file.

## After

One match names `$crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions ask research static IP` because the answer leaves that question open. It adds the spec, as in `orders static IP`, only when those words would match more than one spec.

- One or two sentences: `$crav1-spark-to-spec`
- A pile of ideas and technical hunches: `$crav1-ideas-to-spec`
- Several features, or mixed files: `$crav1-bundle-to-specs`

Production follows `$crav1-read-environment`: shape and connections only, after the same yes or no.
